operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are mixed-case with underscores (Ref_Document_Types, Document_Type_Code); must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
Tiny DB: max table 15 rows (Documents, Accounts), most 2-5; original_values lists are short, so rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) often returns all rows.
Document_Date declared DATETIME, storage class text, format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (e.g. '2004-08-28 06:59:19'); ts_fuzzer dispatch: contains 'date' -> first element parses as int? no -> Date fuzzer.
Document_Description and Other_Details are 100% NULL (distinct=0, storage ['null']); original_values are all None; String sampler drops None -> empty elements -> p:=1 (always fresh).
Statements.Statement_ID is BOTH the PK and an FK to Documents.Document_ID (self-ish chain, not self-table); table order must place Documents before Statements.
Documents_with_Expenses.Document_ID is PK and FK to Documents.Document_ID; Accounts.Statement_ID FK to Statements.Statement_ID (which is itself an FK).
All FKs point to existing parents with unique PKs; no dangling FKs, no composite keys, no self-references within a table.
CHAR(15) columns (Document_Type_Code, Budget_Type_Code) dispatch to String fuzzer with length=15; values are short codes ('BK','CV','GV','ORG','SF').
INTEGER PKs (Project_ID, Document_ID, Statement_ID, Account_ID) dispatch to Number fuzzer; samples are small ints (7..240), not sequential.
Account_Details is VARCHAR but stores numeric-looking strings ('495.063','12223.93'); String fuzzer will treat as text, not Number.
No views, triggers, or indexes beyond PKs in the DDL; empty clone is cheap.
Document_Type_Description has distinct=4 < rows=5 (a duplicate 'good'/'excellent' style value); not a unique column, so drop_unique_duplicates won't fire.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on Document_Date: template inferred from first parsable element -> '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; range from min/max parsed dates (~1970..2012); fresh dates uniform in that range, formatted with template.

String fuzzer on Document_Type_Code / Budget_Type_Code: length range from elements (2-3 chars) up to 15; fresh strings over a-zA-Z0-9() plus contaminate; likely produces codes not in the 3-5 real values -> FN on equality joins to Ref_* tables unless FK fill copies parent values.
String fuzzer on Document_Description / Other_Details: all-None originals -> p=1, always fresh random strings; any query filtering these on real values will miss (FN).

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: range [-10^0,10^0]=[-1,1]? scale=0 -> [-1,1] plus perturbation; but list range uses min(el)..max(el)+1 overwritten to full max -> fresh draws near 0/1, far from real 7..240 -> FN on range predicates, FP on ties.

FK fill: Documents.Document_Type_Code draws from Ref_Document_Types.Document_Type_Code final values (5 codes) with replacement -> duplicates in Documents; Documents.Project_ID from Projects (5 values) -> duplicates; realistic join cardinalities preserved.

Statements.Statement_ID is PK+FK: drawn from Documents.Document_ID final values, then PK-dedup keeps first occurrence -> Statements may shrink to 1-2 rows; Accounts.Statement_ID then draws from that small set.
Documents_with_Expenses.Document_ID PK+FK to Documents: drawn from Documents final IDs, PK-dedup; Budget_Type_Code from Ref_Budget_Codes (3 values) -> heavy duplication.
choose_table_sizes: w.p. 0.5 flat ~30-230 rows per table, else level-based (level0 1-31, next x4 capped 2500) -> Ref_* tables may get 30+ rows vs real 3-5, inflating join results (FP on COUNT).

NOT NULL not enforced in Python: String sampler can emit None? (no, drops None) but Number/Date fresh draws are non-null; PK/unique dedup may still leave rows that violate FK if parent empty -> insert fails, row skipped (writedb).
Known miss drivers: FN from implausible fresh strings/numbers on low-cardinality code columns; FP from missing ties (real 5 codes vs 30+ generated) and from Date range mismatch on 'year' predicates.
